original_question: Let X be a projective manifold with large algebraic fundamental group, and let L be an ample line bundle on X. Given a positive number N, does there exist a finite etale cover p : X' -> X such that either (1) the Seshadri number of p^*L at every point of X' is greater than N, or (2) the Seshadri number along the diagonal D' subset X' x X' of p_e^*(p_1^*L tensor p_2^*L) is greater than N? If neither statement is always true, what condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees a positive answer?
target_in_paper: Section 2.6, Problem 2.6.2 ("Algebraic fundamental groups and Seshadri numbers"), p. 7, with the immediately preceding Proposition 2.6.1 on p. 7 supplying the motivating context.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target: it has the right ambient objects (a projective manifold X, an ample line bundle L, and a positive parameter N), the right kind of conclusion (existence of a finite étale cover), the two intended Seshadri-growth questions (pointwise on X' and along the diagonal in X' × X'), and the paper's final follow-up asking for an additional condition on the fundamental group if the first two questions fail or remain unresolved.
missing_details: The exact target is not a theorem or conjecture but the open Problem 2.6.2 in Section 2.6; Proposition 2.6.1 is only the motivating nearby result.

The hypothesis "X has large algebraic fundamental group" should be defined exactly as in the paper: for every irreducible subvariety Z ⊂ X with normalization ν: Z^ν → X, the image of ν_* on algebraic fundamental groups hat pi_1(Z^ν) → hat pi_1(X) is infinite.
The paper immediately states an equivalent reformulation of that hypothesis: the algebraic universal cover of X contains no complete subvariety.
Problem 2.6.2 asks parts (1) and (2) separately, not as a single either/or statement; the finite étale cover may depend on N, and the cover used in (1) need not be the same as the one used in (2).

In part (2), one must define p-tilde := p × p: X' × X' → X × X, D' ⊂ X' × X' as the diagonal, and p_1, p_2: X × X → X as the two projections; otherwise the notation in the diagonal Seshadri question is ambiguous.
The line bundle in part (2) is exactly p-tilde^*(p_1^*L ⊗ p_2^*L), and the Seshadri number is taken along D', not merely 'on the product' in some unspecified sense.
To be stand-alone, it helps to unpack 'projective manifold' as 'smooth projective variety,' which is the paper's ambient meaning.
The paper's final clause is phrased precisely as: if the answer to (1) or (2) is negative or unclear, what condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees a positive answer?

The omitted nearby context is Proposition 2.6.1: from the large algebraic fundamental group hypothesis, the paper already gets a finite étale cover p: X' → X such that for every irreducible subvariety W ⊂ X', one has (p^*L)^(dim W) · W > N; Problem 2.6.2 asks whether this can be strengthened to Seshadri lower bounds.
refined_question: Let X be a projective manifold (smooth projective variety) with large algebraic fundamental group, meaning that for every irreducible subvariety Z ⊂ X with normalization ν: Z^ν → X, the image of ν_*: hat pi_1(Z^ν) → hat pi_1(X) is infinite. Let L be an ample line bundle on X, and let N > 0. (1) Does there exist a finite étale cover p: X' → X such that the Seshadri number ε(p^*L; x) is greater than N for every point x ∈ X'? (2) Does there exist a finite étale cover p: X' → X such that, writing p-tilde := p × p: X' × X' → X × X, letting D' ⊂ X' × X' be the diagonal, and letting p_1, p_2: X × X → X be the two projections, the Seshadri number of p-tilde^*(p_1^*L ⊗ p_2^*L) along D' is greater than N? (3) If the answer to (1) or (2) is negative or unclear, what additional condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees an affirmative answer?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent hypothesis only: replace "X has large algebraic fundamental group" by "the algebraic universal cover of X contains no complete subvariety," and ask the same three-part question.
justification: The draft is aimed at Problem 2.6.2 almost verbatim, not at a neighboring statement elsewhere in the paper. Section 2.6 first defines "large algebraic fundamental group" and states its equivalent reformulation in terms of the algebraic universal cover, then gives Proposition 2.6.1 as motivation, and immediately after that records the exact three-part open problem your draft is paraphrasing. The only substantive drift in the draft is that it merges parts (1) and (2) into an either/or question, whereas the paper asks them separately and only then asks in part (3) for an additional condition on the fundamental group if either one is negative or unclear.
